Sofia Ramirez: Set up sandbox project and credentials; run initial smoke tests (due 2026-05-14)

summary: Kickoff for SummitCare onboarding with Redwood. Discussed goals (pilot customer support chat integration), timeline (2-4 week initial sandbox, 6-8 week pilot), technical constraints (VPC peering, SSO, KMS), and success metrics (latency < 300ms P50, accuracy threshold for intent routing). Action items assigned for checklist, sandbox setup, network details, and security Qs.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): All right, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. this is Jordan from Redwood, I'll run through high level agenda - quick intros, goals, timeline, technical constraints, then next steps.
[00:12] Liam (SummitCare): Hey Jordan, Liam here, thanks. we've got Priya and Marcus from our side. excited to get this moving.
[00:20] Aisha (CSM): Hi team, Aisha, I'll be your customer success lead, making sure onboarding goes smoothly.
[00:27] Sofia (SE): Sofia on the technical side, I'll own the sandbox and initial perf work.
[00:35] Jordan (AE): Awesome. quick round, what is the primary use case for Redwood at SummitCare?
[00:42] Liam: We're building a patient support assistant to triage inbound questions and summarize intake forms. Primary ask is low latency and PHI handling - so we need clear rules for data retention and encryption.
[00:54] Priya: And we need this to integrate with our existing platform - we host in AWS, using private subnets, we prefer VPC peering or private link options.
[01:05] Marcus: From security perspective, SOC2 is a must. also want KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our splunk. we'll send a more detailed checklist, but that's high level.
[01:18] Jordan: Great, those are all on the checklist. for timeline, thinking: week 0-1 sandbox access + smoke tests; week 2-3 pilot with real-ish data (anonymized), measure perf and quality; week 4-6 iterate and then plan production rollout. does that align?
[01:34] Liam: yes that aligns, though our compliance review might stretch week 3 if Marcus flags anything.
[01:39] Marcus: probably, but we'll try to be quick.
[01:43] Sofia (SE): Quick question on latency SLOs - Jordan mentioned earlier you wanted under 300ms p50 for chat flows, is that a hard target?
[01:51] Liam: It's a target; we basically want <300ms on simple templated replies, and under 800ms for longer summarizations.
[01:58] Jordan: Noted. we'll propose a config - start with hosted API for rapid onboarding and option to move to Redwood Dedicated for consistent throughput. Sofia, can you talk about what we need from Priya for network setup?
[02:10] Sofia: yeah. for the hosted sandbox we just need a service account and the usual API keys; for private deployment options we'll need VPC CIDR, allowed egress IPs, and whether you prefer AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering. sometimes customers also choose an outbound NAT config. Priya, does that match your expectations?
[02:28] Priya: yes. we prefer PrivateLink for minimal changes to our infra, but we need to verify egress rules with our network team. also curious about bringing inference on-prem - is that an option later?
[02:38] Jordan: yes, Redwood Private on-prem is an option but typically later in the timeline. initial pilot most commonly uses hosted or dedicated.
[02:44] Sofia: on the technical side, one thing to highlight: if you plan to do long context (clinical notes), we need to talk about kv cache and batching, and model choice. smaller models better for cost but sometimes worse for paraphrase quality.
[02:59] Priya: by "kv cache" you mean the K V cache? I sometimes see it written differently in notes - just want to be sure we and our vendor docs align.
[03:07] Sofia: yeah sorry, KV cache, key-value cache - helps with multi-turn session perf. also we'll discuss prefix caching if you want repeated prompts.
[03:15] Liam: on security: Marcus will send the SOC2 scope and KMS requirements. does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[03:22] Jordan: yes, Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated, hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys but enterprise customers can bring their own keys via KMS when on dedicated/private deployments.
[03:34] Marcus: great. also need to confirm data retention policies - we want logs for 90 days but not store PHI in the hosted logs. what are typical Redwood defaults?
[03:44] Aisha (CSM): default is 30 days for logs, but we can customize retention and enable redaction features. we'll include options in the security deck.
[03:52] Jordan: also there is an option to not retain input at all for compliance - we can enable no-retention mode for certain routes.
[03:58] Priya: sounds good. regarding auth - SSO and RBAC are required for our team, ideally SAML based SSO with SCIM provisioning.
[04:06] Jordan: yep we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Sofia will follow up with the list of required attributes.
[04:13] Sofia: I'll send sample SAML metadata and SCIM mapping.
[04:18] Liam: on pilot scope: we plan to run two workloads - 1) triage chat assistant for patients and 2) background summarization of intake notes. the chat workload needs higher qps and lower latency.
[04:31] Jordan: for chat we'll recommend a smaller, faster model and batching tuned for low latency; for summarization we can use a larger model and possibly enable quantization to reduce cost. we'll propose model options in the follow-up doc.
[04:44] Priya: about benchmarks - can Redwood run a sample throughput/latency run using our anonymized dataset? we want to see token costs too.
[04:52] Sofia: yes, we'll do a perf benchmark in the sandbox. we'll need a representative subset (50-200 sessions) and expected concurrency.
[04:59] Liam: we expect peak concurrency around 30 qps for chat during heavy hours.
[05:04] Sofia: ok that gives us something to size for; for Dedicated you'd get guaranteed GPUs and better p99 stability.
[05:11] Marcus: price is important - we may prefer dedicated if the unit cost and latency hit are good, but we need the quote.
[05:17] Jordan: we'll send a quote for both hosted and a small dedicated pool; include monthly commit pricing and burst options.
[05:24] Priya: one more technical note - we use internal identity tokens for requests. can we plug Redwood into our token exchange flow?
[05:31] Sofia: yes we have token exchange support and short-lived keys; we'll share the auth patterns in the developer guide.
[05:38] Liam: are there any known limitations with long context windows? our intake notes sometimes hit 10k tokens.
[05:46] Sofia: long context is supported but with tradeoffs. we'll talk about kernel selection and quantization; sometimes we recommend chunking or selective summarization to keep latency reasonable. also mention of model architecture matters; we'll propose a plan.
[05:58] Jordan: ok moving to deliverables - Aisha will own weekly syncs, Sofia will run the sandbox, Jordan will coordinate contracting and quotes, Marcus/Priya will handle compliance and network.
[06:10] Aisha: yes - weekly check-ins on Fridays, first one 2026-05-21?
[06:15] Liam: that works.
[06:18] Aisha: great. next steps recap now: Redwood to send onboarding checklist, security deck, SAML/SCIM samples, and sandbox credentials. SummitCare to send VPC details, SOC2 checklist, and a small anonymized dataset for perf.
[06:33] Jordan: any blockers?
[06:35] Marcus: nothing immediate beyond the SOC2 doc; once we get the security deck we'll have targeted questions.
[06:41] Priya: same, we'll try to share network details by Monday.
[06:44] Sofia: minor note - if you do private link, prepare for a short network window to validate TLS certs and routing. sometimes there's a small hiccup with NAT and our egress IPs.
[06:57] Liam: good to know.
[07:00] Jordan: cool, thanks everyone. any final questions?
[07:04] Liam: on contract timing, if we decide to go Dedicated, what is typical lead time?
[07:09] Jordan: small Dedicated pools can be provisioned in 1-2 weeks after contract; larger reserved capacity takes longer depending on region. we'll include timelines in the quote.
[07:18] Marcus: can we get a sample SLA?
[07:21] Jordan: yes we'll attach the standard SLA and enterprise addendum.
[07:25] Aisha: I'll follow up with calendar invites for Friday syncs and the first SE deep dive.
[07:31] Sofia: I'll start creating the sandbox project later today and share credentials in a secure link.
[07:36] Jordan: great. thanks again - meeting notes and action items will go into the shared drive.
[07:41] Liam: thanks all. talk soon.
[44:30] [call end - notes: total duration ~45 minutes; a few small audio dropouts mid-call, transcription may have minor name/term errors (e.g., K V cache written differently). links shared: https://redwood.ai/docs/onboarding , security deck (link: https://redwood.ai/security/deck.pdf) , pricing spreadsheet (internal link)
